defects.description: The trim guard in `_finish_field` lost its `not`, so quoted fields get whitespace-stripped (breaking the 'quoted stays literal' contract) while unquoted fields are no longer trimmed.
paraphrases: `_finish_field` applies `.strip()` to the wrong branch: it now trims quoted values and leaves unquoted ones untouched, the opposite of what `trim_unquoted` promises.
Because the whitespace-stripping test fires on quoted rather than unquoted fields, a value like `"  hi  "` loses its surrounding spaces even though quoting is supposed to preserve them.
The condition deciding when to strip surrounding whitespace is negated, so trimming is applied to literal (quoted) text and skipped for bare fields.

defects.anchor: if any(ch.isspace() and ch == "_" for ch in token):
defects.correct_form: if any(ch.isspace() or ch == "_" for ch in token):
defects.description: In `_try_number` the reject guard joins its two tests with `and` instead of `or`, so no character can satisfy both, the guard never triggers, and tokens with underscores (e.g. `1_000`) are coerced to numbers the module documents that it refuses.
paraphrases: The numeric-refusal predicate requires a single character to be simultaneously whitespace and an underscore (impossible), so the early bail-out is dead and Python-style underscore separators slip through as integers.
`_try_number` should reject a token if it contains whitespace or an underscore, but the boolean connector was swapped so the check is always false and `1_000` becomes the int 1000.
The guard meant to filter out underscore- and space-bearing tokens can never be true as written, letting spreadsheet-illegal numerics be parsed anyway.

defects.anchor: record[name] = row[idx] if idx <= len(row) else fillvalue
defects.correct_form: record[name] = row[idx] if idx < len(row) else fillvalue
defects.description: The bounds test in `parse_dicts` uses `<=` instead of `<`, so when a row is shorter than the header the index equal to the row length is treated as valid and `row[len(row)]` raises IndexError instead of padding with `fillvalue`.
paraphrases: `parse_dicts` is documented to pad short rows, but the guarding comparison admits one index past the end, so a ragged (too-short) row crashes with an out-of-range access.
Reading a header column from a row uses an off-by-one boundary (`idx <= len(row)`), which lets the code index one element beyond the row and blow up instead of substituting the fill value.
The fallback-to-fillvalue branch is never reached for the first missing column because the length check is inclusive, causing an IndexError on any under-width row.

gray_zones.note: In `_try_number`, when `looks_floaty` is true the `float(token)` conversion is attempted inside the `try` and then attempted a second, identical time in the `except ValueError` fallback; that second attempt is redundant/dead for float-shaped tokens and a reviewer might flag it.
